ORDER Heard on IA No.3890/2019, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act moved on behalf of appellants for condonation of delay.
2. On due consideration and for the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed.
Delay in filing the instant appeal is hereby condoned.

3. This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 11.10.2018 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Datia (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.42/2018, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Datia (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10775 2 MA-4484-2019 4.
The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.

The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
5.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to death of Rona Devi Sahu in the motor accident,
the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.9,57,700/- along with interest from the Munnalal Sahu vs Balram Kushwah on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157196043/
1 date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

6. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have preferred the present appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal has passed the award without proper appreciation of the evidence and settled principles of law.
It is contended that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the appellants indicate that prior to the accident, the deceased, aged about 75 years, was running a papad business and allegedly earning Rs.40,000/- per month while also being an income tax assessee.
However, the Claims Tribunal failed to properly appreciate these aspects and assessed the monthly income of the deceased at only Rs.4,000/-, which is grossly inadequate.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal has erred in not awarding just and reasonable compensation under conventional heads such as loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses.
Hence, enhancement of compensation has been prayed for.
6. On the other hand, learned counsels for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10775 3 MA-4484-2019 7.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.

8. Upon careful scrutiny of the record, it is evident that the claimants have failed to produce cogent and reliable documentary evidence, such as income tax returns, account books, or other independent proof, to substantiate the claim of monthly income of Rs.40,000/-.
However, it cannot be ignored that the deceased was self-employed and engaged in a small-scale business (papad making and selling), which would reasonably generate some steady income.

Considering the age of the deceased (75 years), the nature of work, prevailing minimum wages, and the fact that even in the absence of strict proof, some reasonable estimation is permissible in motor accident claims, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs. 6,000/- per month.

This assessment strikes a balance between the absence of strict proof and the probability of continued earning from a small business.
9.
As regard to loss of income including future prospects, claimants are not entitled for any future prospects as the deceased was aged 75 years at the time of accident.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 5 be applied.

Therefore, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal up to this extent be set aside and the reasonable NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10775 4 MA-4484-2019 amount of compensation be awarded adding reasonable amount of compensation under loss of consortium,
loss of estate and other heads etc.
Munnalal Sahu vs Balram Kushwah on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157196043/
2 10.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   Income Rs.6000 x   After deducting Dependency 1/2 Rs.36,000/
 Multiplier 5 Rs.1,80,00
Other Heads:-

Medical Bill Rs.7,07,70  Transportation Rs.20,000/
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-

Total Compensation = Rs.10,57,700/-
11.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.10,57,700/- as against the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
12. In the result, miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified, and the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellants in the present appeal.
It is made clear that the appellants shall not be entitled to interest for the period from 09.01.2019 to 01.04.2026.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10775 5 MA-4484-2019 copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

13 . In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.

14. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands partly allowed and disposed of.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
